group.title: Problems and plans
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: One of the things you can choose.
examples: We have two {options}: wait or take a taxi.
wrong: There is only one option, so we have lots to choose from.

words.meaning: Another thing you can choose or use instead.
examples: If the train is full, the bus is a good {alternative}.
wrong: There is no alternative, so we can pick any other way.

words.meaning: A way to deal with a problem.
examples: We found a {solution} to the parking problem.
wrong: His solution made the problem much worse and solved nothing.

words.meaning: To find the answer to a problem.
examples: Can you {solve} this puzzle?
wrong: I solved the puzzle, but I never found the answer.

words.meaning: Something done or said wrongly.
examples: There’s an {error} in the bill: we paid twice.
wrong: The report has an error, so every part is correct.

words.meaning: What you hope to achieve.
examples: My {aim} is to run a marathon next year.
wrong: His aim is to win, so he doesn’t want to win.

words.meaning: A choice you make after thinking about it.
examples: Moving abroad was a big {decision}.
wrong: She made her decision, so she still hasn’t chosen.

words.meaning: To move an event to a later time.
examples: The match was {postponed} because of the rain.
wrong: They postponed the party, so it happened a week earlier.

words.meaning: To repair something or put a problem right.
examples: Can you {fix} my bike before the weekend?
wrong: He fixed the broken lamp, so it still doesn’t work.

words.meaning: The reason why something is done or made.
examples: What is the {purpose} of your visit?
wrong: The purpose of a key is to tell the time.

words.meaning: Something that stops you or makes progress hard.
examples: Money is the biggest {obstacle} to our plan.
wrong: The fallen tree was an obstacle that made the road easier.

words.meaning: A problem, or the fact that something is hard.
examples: She had {difficulty} finding the house.
wrong: He found the house with great difficulty, as easily as anything.

words.meaning: To deal successfully with something hard.
examples: How do you {cope} with so much work?
wrong: He coped well, so he couldn’t deal with anything.

words.meaning: To succeed in dealing with a problem or fear.
examples: She {overcame} her fear of flying.
wrong: He overcame his fear, so he is still too scared to fly.

words.meaning: To get ready, or make something ready, for a future event.
examples: I need to {prepare} for tomorrow’s interview.
wrong: She prepared for the exam by doing nothing until it started.

words.meaning: Something that goes very badly or causes great harm.
examples: The party was a {disaster}: the food burned and nobody came.
wrong: The trip was a disaster, so everything went perfectly.

words.meaning: To stop for a moment because you are not sure.
examples: Don’t {hesitate} to call me if you need help.
wrong: He hesitated and answered straight away with no pause.

words.meaning: A try at doing something, often hard.
examples: He passed the test on his second {attempt}.
wrong: She made no attempt, so she tried three times.

words.meaning: To do what you tried or planned to do.
examples: She {succeeded} in getting the job.
wrong: He succeeded, so he didn’t get what he wanted.

words.meaning: A lack of success.
examples: The first plan was a {failure}, so we tried again.
wrong: The show was a failure, so everyone loved it.

words.meaning: The chance that something bad will happen.
examples: There is a {risk} of rain, so take an umbrella.
wrong: There is no risk at all, so it is very dangerous.

words.meaning: A second plan to use if the first one fails.
examples: If it rains, our {backup plan} is the cinema.
wrong: Our backup plan was the first thing we tried.

words.meaning: Trying different ways until you find one that works.
examples: I learned to cook by {trial and error}.
wrong: She solved it by trial and error, getting it right on the very first try.

words.meaning: Slowly, doing one stage at a time.
examples: Follow the instructions {step by step}.
wrong: He did it step by step, all at once in one go.

words.meaning: To think about the good and bad sides before deciding.
examples: {Weigh up} the costs before you buy a car.
wrong: She weighed up both choices without thinking about either.

words.meaning: To wait until the next day before you decide.
examples: Don’t decide now; {sleep on it}.
wrong: I’ll sleep on it, so I’ll give you my answer right now.

words.meaning: To make a new decision different from the old one.
examples: I wanted pizza, but I {changed my mind}.
wrong: He changed his mind, so his decision stayed the same.

words.meaning: Done because you wanted to, not by accident.
examples: She broke the vase {on purpose} because she was angry.
wrong: He did it on purpose; it was a total accident.

words.meaning: Done without meaning to.
examples: I took your umbrella {by mistake}.
wrong: She deleted the file by mistake, exactly as she had planned.

words.meaning: Before the time when something happens.
examples: Book your tickets {in advance}.
wrong: We paid in advance, after the concert was over.

words.meaning: To not happen in the way you planned.
examples: Everything {went wrong} on our first day.
wrong: Nothing went right, so the plan didn’t go wrong.

words.meaning: Something that might happen or be true.
examples: There’s a {possibility} that the flight will be late.
wrong: There is no possibility of rain, so it will surely rain.

words.meaning: An idea or plan you offer for others to think about.
examples: Do you have any {suggestions} for the party?
wrong: His suggestion was an order that everyone had to follow.

words.meaning: The thing you try only when everything else has failed.
examples: Calling a locksmith is our {last resort}.
wrong: As a last resort, we tried it first before anything else.

words.meaning: Without meaning to; by chance.
examples: I {accidentally} sent the message to my boss.
wrong: She accidentally broke it after planning to for weeks.

words.meaning: Surprising because you did not think it would happen.
examples: We had an {unexpected} visitor last night.
wrong: The visit was unexpected because we had planned it for months.

words.meaning: Difficult and needing care to deal with.
examples: Parking here can be {tricky} on a Saturday.
wrong: The question was tricky, so everyone answered it in a second.

words.meaning: Not sure or not known yet.
examples: I’m {uncertain} about which job to take.
wrong: He was uncertain, so he knew exactly what to do.

words.meaning: To think about and prepare for the future.
examples: If you {plan ahead}, the trip will be easier.
wrong: He plans ahead by deciding everything at the last minute.

words.meaning: To have the opposite result to the one you wanted.
examples: His plan to save money {backfired} and cost him more.
wrong: The plan backfired, so it worked exactly as we hoped.
